comment: TL Part 5: the week 1 lunch (school_calendar story w1_lunch_friends), daytime scenes for the school-hours townsfolk (their npc daytimeScene, played the first time you talk to them during school hours) and skip hangouts with the Core Four (skip_<id>, from a 'skip with me?' text).

steps.text: Lunch
The cafeteria is loud. Two seats are open: one next to Dex, one across from Theo.

steps.speaker: dex
steps.text: Okay, new kid. Important question. Is the mystery meat chicken? I say it's a philosophy.

steps.speaker: theo
steps.text: It's turkey. Statistically. I checked the delivery labels... that's a weird thing to say out loud, isn't it.
Where do you sit?

steps.speaker: dex
steps.text: Excellent choice. You get the seat with the wobbly leg. It builds character.
Dex spends lunch teaching you three ways to flick a grape. Two of them work.

steps.speaker: theo
steps.text: Oh. Hi. You can, um. Sit. Do you want to see a diagram? You don't have to see the diagram.
The diagram is about why the hallway lights flicker on the third floor. It's a good diagram.

steps.speaker: dex
steps.text: A merger! Theo, you're our treasurer now.

steps.speaker: theo
steps.text: I don't... okay. I'd be a good treasurer, actually.
For one lunch, the three of you take up way too much room.
Officer Pruitt
A woman in a pressed uniform checks her clipboard, then checks you.

steps.speaker: officer_pruitt
steps.text: School hours. You know what that means, and so do I.

steps.speaker: officer_pruitt
steps.text: I'm not here to ruin your life. I'm here so nobody wanders into the woods in the middle of a Tuesday. People do, around here.

steps.speaker: officer_pruitt
steps.text: Go on. I didn't see you. Once.
Rae
The corner store bell jingles. The clerk doesn't look up from her magazine.

steps.speaker: rae
steps.text: Skipping? Same. Well, I skipped permanently. Two years ago.

steps.speaker: rae
steps.text: Want the real news? Every kid who went missing was last seen by the woods. Nobody at school will say it. I'll say it.
Walt
An old man tosses bread crumbs to pigeons that seem to know him.

steps.speaker: walt
steps.text: You've got the look. Same look I had, thirty years back, the night the fountain ran.

steps.speaker: walt
steps.text: Water came up red as a sunset. Next morning the last train left, and it never came back.

steps.speaker: walt
steps.text: Nobody believes me. Pigeons do.
Mo
A delivery van idles at the curb. The driver waves you over.

steps.speaker: mo
steps.text: I drive every street in this town, every day. You notice things.

steps.speaker: mo
steps.text: Like the Mayor's car parked behind the school after hours. Every week. Same night.

steps.speaker: mo
steps.text: Didn't hear it from me. Need a ride sometime, I take snacks as payment.
Mr. Ellis
A man with a teacher's lanyard is hiding behind a newspaper. He lowers it, sees you, and sighs.

steps.speaker: mr_ellis
steps.text: Ah. You're supposed to be in class. I'm supposed to be subbing it.

steps.speaker: mr_ellis
steps.text: Tell you what. If anyone asks, you were with me on an educational errand. Once. I'm a sub, not a saint.
Skipping with Theo
Theo leads you to the roof access stairs, where the hallway lights don't reach.

steps.speaker: theo
steps.text: I've never skipped before. My heart rate is... significant.

steps.speaker: theo
steps.text: But I wanted to show you this. The dust up here doesn't fall. It just hangs. Something holds it up.

steps.speaker: theo
steps.text: I have several working theories. You're the first person I've told any of them to.
Skipping with Mara
Mara finds a bench by the park pond and opens her sketchbook between you.

steps.speaker: mara
steps.text: I couldn't sit in that room today. Everything was too loud.
She draws the pond, the ducks, and then, quietly, you.

steps.speaker: mara
steps.text: It's not finished. Here. You can keep it anyway.
Skipping with Dex
Dex sneaks you out the side door and straight to the arcade, which is, technically, closed.

steps.speaker: dex
steps.text: Okay but hear me out: the owner owes me a favor. Big favor. Medium favor. He knows my face.

steps.speaker: dex
steps.text: Here's the thing. I joke a lot. You noticed. Sometimes it's because the real stuff is... a lot.

steps.speaker: dex
steps.text: Anyway! Two tokens. Loser buys fries.
Skipping with Priya
Priya meets you at the library's back table, armed with three highlighters and a plan.

steps.speaker: priya
steps.text: I'm not skipping. I'm conducting independent research. There's a difference, and I can argue it.

steps.speaker: priya
steps.text: I wanted thirty minutes where nobody expects me to be impressive. You don't, do you?

steps.speaker: priya
steps.text: Good. Then help me with this crossword.
